questions.prompt: `orderItems.Join(products, item => item.ProductId, product => product.Id, ...)` runs over an order item whose `ProductId` matches no product. What happens to that order item?
options: It is returned with `ProductName` set to `null`
It is left out, because `Join` returns only elements with matching keys in both collections
`Join` throws because a key is missing
It is returned in a separate group of unmatched items
questions.explanation: `Join` is an inner join: only elements that have matching keys in both collections are returned, like `INNER JOIN` in SQL.

questions.prompt: `departments.GroupJoin(employees, dept => dept.Id, emp => emp.DepartmentId, (dept, emps) => ...)` runs over a department that has no employees. What does the result contain for it?
options: Nothing; departments without employees are dropped
One entry per employee, with a `null` department
The department with an empty group of employees
The department paired with every employee
questions.explanation: `GroupJoin` groups the matches, and even if there's no match the outer element is still included with an empty group, so every department appears.

questions.prompt: In the left outer join query, what is the job of `from dept in empDeptGroup.DefaultIfEmpty()`?
options: It removes employees whose department is missing
It sorts each employee's departments
It turns the join into an inner join
It keeps employees with no matching department, giving `dept` a null/default value
questions.explanation: A left outer join returns every element of the left collection; when there is no match, the right side is null or default, which is why the query uses `dept != null ? dept.DepartmentName : "N/A"`.

questions.prompt: How does the lesson suggest doing a right outer join in LINQ?
options: Swap the collections and do a left join
Call the built-in `RightJoin` operator
Use `Intersect` on the two collections
Use `GroupJoin` without `into`
questions.explanation: LINQ doesn't support a right join directly, but you can swap the collections and do a left join; a full outer join is simulated with a left join, a right join and `Union`.

questions.prompt: `seq1` is `{1, 2, 3}` and `seq2` is `{2, 3, 4}`. Which call returns only `{1}`?
options: `seq1.Intersect(seq2)`
`seq1.Union(seq2)`
`seq1.Except(seq2)`
`seq2.Except(seq1)`
questions.explanation: `Except` returns elements in the first sequence but not in the second. `Intersect` would give `{2, 3}`, `Union` `{1, 2, 3, 4}`, and `seq2.Except(seq1)` `{4}`.

source.section: #### `Except` — Elements in the first but not in the second
